newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip on low demand, seen in range.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip on low demand, seen in range.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased in late afternoon trading and dealers said they saw levels fluctuating at current levels for the next few days on weak western demand and pessimism about the Russian economy.
They said the market would close lower but little changed.

"Our overseas friends hadn't quite woken up today and domestic investors orient themselves on western operators," said senior Trinfiko trader Grigory Pensky. "If there is growth tomorrow then it will be very small, around one percent."

Yevgeny Skibitsky, head trader at Rossiisky Kredit Bank, said comments by First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais that the Russian economy still had many serious problems despite gains would not encourage Western clients.
"The fact that Chubais said the situation in the Russian economy is bad will not stimulate investors to active participation in the Russian market," he said.

Traders differed on the effect of announcements earlier in the day that Russia had set $1.18 billion as the starting price for an auction of 25 percent plus one share of state holding company Svyazinvest.
"So far the market hasn't reacted at all," said Trinfiko's Pensky. "As it stood, so it stands."
A senior privatisation official said the auction, previously scheduled for mid-May, would now likely take place in June.

But Skibitsky said international long-distance provider Rostelekom could see a depreciation in share price in connection with the transfer of the state's 38 percent -- or 51 percent of voting shares -- stake to Svyazinvest.
"I can confirm that Svyazinvest shares are becoming more attractive than those of Rostelekom," he said, calling a drop in Rostelekom's price realistic.
Rostelekom eased to $3.85 from $3.86 on Monday. Svyazinvest is not traded on the RTS.

Shares in oil producer Tomskneft, which announced 1996 net profit calculated to Russian standards on an accruals basis of 208.1 billion roubles, were untraded on Tuesday, after closing on May 22 at $10.95. Tomskneft reported 1995 net profit calculated on a cash basis was 62.6 billion roubles.
National electricity company and market benchmark UES slipped to $0.3190 from $0.3198.
